answer: Each identity is anchored to one vertex, and depth beneath it is earned only with locked, non-transferable work credit: 400 credits held for 20 epochs. At joining, the credit is dyed with a unique pigment ratio and bound to a ferrous tracer whose signature is recorded at that vertex. It cannot be split, lent, or shown for two identities. A farm of 1,000 must lock 400,000 credits and forge 1,000 distinct tracers, since copies share one signature. Auditors re-scan tracers each epoch; any duplicate signature, pigment mismatch, or tracer at two vertices slashes the lock and erases the depth.
